text:
Noah Patel: Dropping ADR draft for review: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ARCH/ADR-041+-+Hardware+tuning+profiles+pack  
Main decisions: versioned profile pack artifact, selection in runtime, overrides w/ guardrails, rollback plan. Would love eyes esp on config drift + pin semantics.

Architecture Bot: Noah Patel posted a link: ADR-041 - Hardware tuning profiles pack (DRAFT)

Quentin Harris: Reading now. First reaction: we need to be super explicit about what is “versioned” (profile pack vs runtime build vs control plane defaults). Right now ADR says “pack is versioned” but doesn’t define how we prevent config drift between (a) pack in repo, (b) pack in hosted control plane, and (c) private installs via Helm.

Mateo Alvarez: +1. We got burned before with “defaults live in 3 places”. I’m ok w/ selection logic in runtime, but the source of truth for the actual profile definitions needs to be one.

Ethan Park: Agree. From CP perspective: today we already have fleet defaults in the control plane config service. If pack lives in runtime repo, Hosted still needs a mechanism to roll forward/back the pack separately from binary deploys OR we accept that pack changes are coupled to runtime release trains.

Connor O'Brien: From release eng: coupling is fine if we’re disciplined. I’d prefer “pack version is shipped with runtime-1.22.x” and we can hotfix by releasing 1.22.1, 1.22.2, etc. The alternative (runtime reads arbitrary pack artifact from CP) is more flexible but much higher risk of drift.

Sean Gallagher: SRE angle: decoupled pack scares me unless we have very tight rollback and provenance. We need to know exactly what profile knobs were active when p99 blew up. If CP can change pack out-of-band, on-call needs that in the debug bundle + audit trail.

Allison Grant: +1. If pack is dynamic, metrics must include `profile_pack_version` and ideally a hash/digest. Otherwise correlating perf regressions is going to be a mess.

Benji Okafor: Guardrails section feels under-specified. We should define hard constraints vs soft constraints. E.g. “cannot set kv_cache_headroom < X on L40S” should be hard reject, not warn.

Omar El-Sayed: Also fragmentation / compaction knobs: there are combos that look “valid” but are known-bad (compaction threshold too low + high concurrency => compaction storms). We should encode those as invalid in schema validation.

Quentin Harris: Re drift: propose ADR states:
- Single source of truth: profile definitions live in a versioned artifact generated from the runtime repo (e.g., `profiles/v1.0.0.yaml`), embedded in runtime at build time.
- Control plane can only *select* among versions that are already present in the deployed runtime (or pin “default” vs “explicit”).
That gives us “selection is dynamic” but “definitions aren’t”.

Ethan Park: That’s workable. CP would pass `profile_pack_version` and maybe `profile_override_id` (or “none”). Runtime rejects if it doesn’t have that pack version.

Mateo Alvarez: This is basically what we discussed in eng-runtime: control plane chooses “pack vX + profile_id Y”, runtime ensures compatibility + logs. Good.

Sahana Iyer: + CI gating: if profiles are embedded in runtime, we can run schema validation + golden snapshot in CI (block merges). If profiles are fetched at runtime, CI coverage becomes trickier.

Connor O'Brien: Exactly. Also for rollback: if pack is embedded, rollback = roll back runtime deployment (standard), or flip kill switch to old selection (if old pack version still present in the deployed binary).

Rafael Mendes: For Hosted canary: we can deploy runtime that contains {v1.0.0, v1.0.1} packs (or default + new), then CP can move the canary cohort between them without redeploy. But that implies runtime supports multiple packs at once.

Noah Patel: ADR currently assumes single pack per runtime build, but we can amend to “runtime may contain N packs” and has deterministic selection. Not sure if that’s too heavy.

Sean Gallagher: Caution: supporting multiple packs sounds great but can lead to “we forgot to remove old pack, now we have a weird long tail of nodes on v1.0.0”. Need explicit lifecycle / LTS policy.

Connor O'Brien: Yeah, release policy needed: e.g. runtime build contains current + previous pack only. LTS branch keeps one. Anything older requires downgrade.

Quentin Harris: Pin semantics: ADR uses “profile_version pin” in overrides. We should distinguish:
- `profile_pack_version` (semantic-ish: 1.0.0)
- `profile_id` (e.g., `h100-sxm-prod-default`)
- Optional `profile_overrides` (guarded, small set)
Also please avoid “profile_version” meaning two different things.

Allison Grant: + in metrics: `profile_pack_version`, `profile_id`, `sku`, `driver`, `cuda`. Not just one “profile_version” label.

Benji Okafor: Rollback: ADR says “kill switch reverts to previous”. Please specify what is reverted:
- selection (profile_id)
- pack version
- or both
Also, who can trigger (SRE on-call? runtime eng?), and where is audit recorded.

Rafael Mendes: +1. We should treat rollback as a first-class action with an audit event. Something like: CP config change emits “profile_selection_change” to audit log w/ actor + reason.

Ethan Park: We already have audit log plumbing for “config update” events in CP. We can extend to include profile selection changes (pack+id). For Private, audit log is local.

Omar El-Sayed: Guardrails request: please add explicit “reject on startup” rules. For example:
- unsupported driver/CUDA combos => refuse to start (or refuse to enable profile pack, fall back?)
- memory headroom check fails => cap concurrency automatically? or refuse override?

Mateo Alvarez: We need a clear fallback story. My take:
- If CP asks for unknown pack version: refuse that selection, fall back to runtime default pack+profile.
- If CP asks for known pack version but incompatible profile_id for detected SKU: refuse and fall back.
- If override breaks safety constraints: hard reject override and fall back.
BUT we must emit a loud log + metric counter so we know it happened.

Sean Gallagher: Prefer hard fail vs silent fallback? Silent fallback can hide misconfig until perf differs. Maybe:
- Hosted: fallback ok but page on “fallback_used > 0” above threshold.
- Private: warn + continue, but surface in installer preflight.

Quentin Harris: ADR should call out “no silent behavior changes”. If fallback happens, it must be visible in:
1) startup log summary
2) /health or /debug endpoint
3) metrics (`profile_selection_fallback_total{reason=...}`)

Allison Grant: + dashboard panel for fallback reasons (unknown_version, incompatible_sku, guardrail_violation, etc.).

Sahana Iyer: Can we codify acceptance: CI unit test validates that every profile_id declares supported SKUs + min driver/CUDA, and that selection is deterministic.

Noah Patel: These are great. I’ll revise ADR with:
- explicit naming (`profile_pack_version`, `profile_id`)
- single source of truth (embedded pack), CP can select only known versions
- guardrails: hard reject list + compatibility checks
- rollback semantics + audit
- “no silent fallback” + required observability

Connor O'Brien: Please add release policy section (what versions ship, LTS/backport expectations). Doesn’t need to be huge but needs to exist.

Mateo Alvarez: +1. Once updated, tag me + Quentin for final review.

Quentin Harris: Sounds good. If you want suggested wording for the drift section, happy to PR text in Confluence.

Noah Patel: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

(reactions) Quentin Harris added :warning: to “decoupled pack scares me unless…”
(reactions) Sean Gallagher added :+1: to “no silent behavior changes”
(reactions) Allison Grant added :bar_chart: to “include hash/digest”
